body:
Decision context from the PLS Neuro JavaFX 25/26 visual comparison for `bd-01M2BEHG491V7SQAVPGMKQNXG5`:

The new stock-Metal capability seam is valuable, but it is not evidence that upgrading JavaFX fixes the visible cortex. In the matched real-surface experiment, JavaFX 25.0.4 and 26.0.2 produced byte-identical `AdaptiveAffineOpaque` frames at 1x and 4x; the stock-Metal smooth result was visually indistinguishable from the patched JavaFX 24 ES2 result; and `ScalarLutInterpolated` was effectively unchanged. `FaceTexelFlat` remains visibly triangulated when zoomed and should not become the default merely because it is numerically simple.

Please keep the issue open beyond the capability checkpoint. The decisive next evidence is the real beta/FIR matrix with matched lateral/medial cameras, failed crops retained, original pick/mapping identities, 20 update-to-painted-frame transitions, and actual latency/resource measurements. Assert `MTLPipeline`, no fallback, no Prism patch, and the packaged module-path closure.

Ownership boundary: renderer-neutral surface plans and scientific identity stay in ScalaFIM shared modules; JavaFX-specific lowering/capability reporting stays in `surface-view-javafx`; PLS Neuro is only the consumer witness. If the visual gate still fails, lodge a separate ScalaFIM JOGL/OpenGL backend issue that consumes the same renderer-neutral plan instead of embedding renderer-specific code in the application.

Evidence: `/Users/bbuchsbaum/code/scala/plsneuro/output/javafx25-26-visual-20260912/README.md` and `comparison.png`.
